title: USE M, ONLY: X => Y — rename-and-import; collisions surface at the use site
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE COMPUTE_HASH(SEED, OUT)
C     'USE M, ONLY :: LOCAL_NAME => MODULE_NAME' imports MODULE_NAME
C     from module M but binds it locally as LOCAL_NAME. If M and
C     this subroutine BOTH define HASH, the unqualified HASH inside
C     the body refers to the LOCAL one, not the module's. A casual
C     reader who scrolls past the USE statement misses the rename.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      USE HASH_LIB, ONLY :: COMPUTE => HASH
      INTEGER SEED, OUT
      INTEGER HASH
      HASH = COMPUTE(SEED)
      OUT  = HASH
      END
notes: USE/ONLY/=> is the F90 way to do qualified imports + rename. A Java rewrite naturally uses `import ... as ...` (Python-style) or fully-qualified names. The spec must capture the rename so the rewrite preserves the actual binding.
